key_insight: First-principles calculations predict β-TeO₃ as an n-type semiconductor with a band gap above 3 eV and work functions reaching approximately 8 eV.
engineering_relevance: This combination could enable transparent electrodes and hole injection, extraction, or transport layers in photovoltaic and light-emitting devices.
method: Calculate electronic properties using first-principles methods.
Assess impurity donors and oxygen-vacancy defects.
Evaluate work functions across low-index nonpolar surfaces.
evidence_signal: Calculations identify several shallow-donor impurities and predict that energetically favored surface oxygen vacancies reduce work functions.
watch_item: The predictions require experimental validation, and preserving ultrahigh work functions demands control of oxygen chemical potential to suppress surface vacancies.
paper_title: Tellurium trioxide as an n-type wide-gap semiconductor with ultrahigh work functions from first principles
